puzzles.title: First Output
puzzles.story: The workshop terminal is waiting for its first message.
puzzles.task: Use printf to greet the world.
hints: The text inside printf's quotes is what the terminal displays.
Fill in the name of the world we are greeting.

puzzles.title: Bonus Points
puzzles.story: A small bonus will bring the score up to the target.
puzzles.task: Set the bonus, add it to the score, and print 15 with printf.
hints: The program starts with a score of 10.
Add 5 to 10 to reach the target of 15.

puzzles.title: Loop Totals
puzzles.story: Add the numbers 1 through 5 to power the workshop.
puzzles.task: Loop from 1 through 5, adding each loop value to total.
hints: The loop stops before its end value, so use 6 to include 5.
Add the loop variable n on every pass.
puzzles.solutionFeedback: The output matches, but add each loop value from 1 through 5. The loop stops before its end value and the loop variable is n.

puzzles.title: Workshop Math
puzzles.story: A pair of gears combine their values to power the next station.
puzzles.task: Multiply the two values and print the result.
hints: The second value is stored in turns.
Three groups of four make 12.

puzzles.title: Signal Code
puzzles.story: The workshop terminal prints the value stored in its signal code.
puzzles.task: Set the code to 42 and print it with printf.
hints: The code is stored in the integer variable code.
Set code to 42.

puzzles.title: Count Up
puzzles.story: The workshop counter needs to report its first three ticks.
puzzles.task: Use a for loop to print 1, 2, and 3 on separate lines.
hints: The loop stops before the limit.
Use 4 to include 1, 2, and 3.

puzzles.title: Power Sum
puzzles.story: Add the first four values to charge the workshop core.
puzzles.task: Loop through 1 to 4, adding each value to total.
hints: The loop limit must be one more than the last value.
Add the current loop value to total each time.

puzzles.title: Square Sequence
puzzles.story: The workshop's calibration sequence sums the first three squares.
puzzles.task: Add n multiplied by itself for n values 1, 2, and 3.
hints: Three values means the loop's exclusive limit is 4.
A square is a number multiplied by itself.

puzzles.title: Reverse Display
puzzles.story: A display counts down by showing the distance from five.
puzzles.task: Loop from 0 to 2 and print 5, 4, and 3.
hints: The loop variable starts at 0 and increases by one.
Subtract the current step from 5.

puzzles.title: Grid Signals
puzzles.story: A two-row grid sends three numbered signals from each row.
puzzles.task: Use nested loops to print 0, 1, 2, 10, 11, and 12.
hints: The outer loop controls two rows; the inner loop controls three columns.
Use limits 2 and 3. The row value is multiplied by 10.
